title: Tiered drug interaction alerts and prescriber response: a ward-randomised trial in three hospitals
abstract: Objective: to compare a tiered drug interaction alert display with the standard display. Design: cluster randomised trial of 36 wards, stratified by hospital and specialty, for six months. Primary outcome: appropriate response to high-severity alerts on a pharmacist-reviewed sample. Balancing outcome: harm from moderate interactions. Results will be written after the trial.
introduction: Prescribers override almost all interaction alerts, including dangerous ones. Tiering improved response to high-severity alerts in one cluster trial, but no study has shown an effect on adverse drug events.
methods: Wards were randomised by the trial statistician, stratified by hospital and specialty. Pharmacists judged appropriateness on monthly random samples, and targeted surveillance covered high-risk moderate combinations in both arms.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present the flow of wards and alerts, the primary comparison with its confidence interval, alert burden, harm surveillance and contamination.
discussion: The discussion will interpret the effect with contamination in mind and weigh it against the harm surveillance. It will state whether tiering should be adopted before the order set change.
limitations: Rotating prescribers may dilute the difference, and reviewers may be unblinded. There is no adverse drug event outcome, and follow-up is six months.
conclusion: To be written after the trial. It will be limited to prescriber response and harm surveillance.
reportingChecklist: CONSORT extension for cluster randomised trials
